product_from_film: Strawberry is a browser with named AI companions that work inside tabs for outreach, recruiting and invoices.
explains_well: Each task has a distinct character and prompt; the recruiting example ends in a candidate table and a request for human input.
unclear: The outreach example shows prepared messages and Send buttons without a clear delivery result or approval boundary.
scenario: Delegate outreach, candidate collection and invoice transfer; answer a question when the agent needs help.
product_clear_basis: The self-driving browser title is visible, followed by companions operating within browser tabs.

categories.finding: Three tasks → human help → customization → company and beta invitation.
The self-driving browser phrase quickly states the category.
The browser title and in-tab typing establish the product in the opening seconds.
Characters enlarge over app windows; cards multiply and table rows appear. Exact paths and easing are unverified.

Rounded pastel characters soften otherwise dense work apps.

categories.finding: Task labels, prompts and output tables make the main sequence readable without sound.
Large characters identify the actor while reframing directs attention to messages and rows.
Each task receives a compact demonstration; the last quarter shifts to funding and access.
The recruiting example pays off with a table and a meaningful user question.
Companion faces suggest friendliness and approachability; no viewer test supports the effect.
The same role name and color follow each companion into its task.
Delivery, invoice accuracy, agent reliability, setup time, funding and current beta availability are unverified.
Named role characters distinguish task types inside an ordinary browser.
Clarify outreach approval and completion.

categories.finding: Give an agent a clear role and a visible question when blocked.
categories.experiment: For Tin, show a campaign agent ask one audience question and continue into a readable output table.

lessons.keep: Tie a named role to its prompt, pointer and output.
try: Show the outreach approval and final status.
For Tin, let a campaign agent ask one clear question before continuing to a readable output.
lessons.avoid: Using a Send button alone as proof of delivery.
lessons.open: Live task success, sending permissions, invoice accuracy and sound remain unverified.

comparison.story: Role-based tasks, human help, customization and invitation.

comparison.texture: Pastel characters over familiar work apps.
comparison.lesson: A visible question explains how an agent returns control to the user.
